title.narrative: Marine Ecosystems for Blue Economy Development Program (Subprogram 1)

description.narrative: The proposed program will support the development of resilient coastal and marine ecosystems and a thriving blue economy in the Philippines. The program aims at (i) integrated and inclusive management of coastal and marine ecosystems; (ii) enhanced management and circularity of plastic and other solid waste; and (iii) strengthened planning, budgeting, and investment in natural capital. The program is aligned with the Philippine Development Plan (PDP) 20232028, the Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC), and the National Adaptation Plan (NAP 2032-2050). It supports a blue economy by harnessing coastal and marine resources, preserving ecosystems, enhancing climate and disaster resilience, and fostering public and sector investment for sustainable growth. The program supports the nature-based development and disaster resilience strategic priority of the country partnership strategy for the Philippines, 20242029. It is aligned with Asian Development Bank's (ADB) Strategy 2030 operational priorities (OPs), specifically (i) OP1 on addressing remaining poverty and reducing inequalities; (ii) OP2 on accelerating progress in gender equality; (iii) OP3 on tackling climate change, building climate and disaster resilience, and enhancing environmental sustainability; (iv) OP5 on rural development and food security; and (v) OP6 on strengthening governance and institutional capacity. The operation is aligned with the Paris Agreement.

Reform area: Plastic and other solid waste management and circularity enhanced
Outcome: At least 10,000 waste sector workers (of which 60% are women) benefit from national and subnational actions under the GAP

(ii) NSWMC will adopt guidelines for LGU implementation of the expanded NEAPP list through their solid waste management plans. (iii) DENR will issue policies on affordable alternatives to SUP, and reduction and refill measures and guidelines for Obliged Enterprises. (iv) DTI will formulate standards and regulations on recycling for packaging and biodegradable content to promote development of alternatives to SUP.

title.narrative: Policy 1 Outcome 1 Implementation Period: Mar 01, 2023 - Sep 30, 2025

description.narrative:
Action 1: To consolidate and promote the development of the blue economy, coastal resources management, and evidence-driven policy, the DENR mandated functions on Ocean Governance within the Department and the Ocean Environment Task Force to prepare an ocean environment policy, establish marine scientific research rules and procedures, and institutionalize oceans ecosystem accounting.
Action 2: To commence implementation of a national framework for blue economy development that adopts the ICM principles:
(i) DENR circulated a draft resolution and draft Joint Memorandum Circular to DILG, DA-BFAR, DOST and DHSUD which shall coordinate and clarify roles and commitments of agencies in blue economy development and ICM. (ii) DILG issued national guidelines for LGUs on the establishment, management, and protection of coastal greenbelts aligned with ICM principles.
Action 3: To align national coastal and marine and biodiversity plans and targets with the Philippines' associated global commitments, DENR updated the abridged PBSAP in outlining specific key targets and indicators in line with the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework 2030.
Action 4: To commence implementation of coastal resilience in line with the joint ICM and Blue Economy objectives through the protection and rehabilitation of mangroves in coastal areas:
(i) DENR and DA-BFAR signed an MOA to adopt an interdepartmental methodology for the assessment of public AUU Fishponds for prospective administrative reversion into mangrove areas. (ii) Department of Agriculture issued a regulation governing the lease of public lands for new fishponds to require mangrove-friendly aquaculture. (iii) DENR issued guidelines on the enrichment planting of mangroves and related activities for biodiversity conservation and coastal resiliency.
Action 5: To enable productive and balanced management of fisheries resources and infrastructure:
(i) The Department of Agriculture, through BFAR, issued instructions for the implementation of Domestic Port Measures Enforcement integrating food safety, stock assessment data collection, and boat licensing and permitting. (ii) PFDA submitted to the Department of Agriculture a draft charter amendment to be considered for inclusion in the legislative agenda to extend PFDA's responsibilities to additional fisheries and agro-industrial commodities.
Action 1: To formalize and embed the institutional framework for blue economy development, DENR will:
(i) Endorse the Blue Economy Bill for approval by Congress to establish a legal framework for national blue economy management. (ii) Adopt the National Ocean Environment Policy. (iii) Commence preparation of national and local marine spatial plans for blue economy development.
Action 2: To cascade the implementation of the ICM approaches to local governments:
(i) DENR and DILG will implement mainstreaming of ICM in comprehensive land use plans and harmonization with local development plans. (ii) DILG will issue guidelines for the mainstreaming of ICM in local development plans. (iii) DILG will support LGUs to implement the guidelines on the coastal greenbelts including the formulation of coastal greenbelt management and action plan integrated into their existing sub-sectoral plans.
Action 3: To broaden the implementation of ecosystem conservation under PBSAP, DENR will increase the coverage of coastal and MPAs.
Action 4: To further strengthen the protection and rehabilitation of mangroves in coastal areas, DENR and DA-BFAR will issue a Joint Administrative Order providing comprehensive guidelines for the assessment methodology of AUU Fishponds with no productive use and the process of their administrative and biophysical reversion from DA-BFAR to DENR and the agreed timelines for reversion.
Action 5: To roll out harmonized management of fishery resources, Department of Agriculture will:
(i) Issue a Unified Fishery Management Ordinance aligned with the National Plan of Action for Small-Scale Fisheries with harvest control measures in the Fishery Management Area 11, Region VI (Western Visayas). (ii) Issue a Fisheries General Memorandum Order to require DA-BFAR regional offices to promote adoption of the ordinance.
Action 6: To enhance sustainable fisheries management and monitoring, the Department of Agriculture will approve and implement the revised PFDA Charter and enforce the DPME System across BFAR operations nationwide through institutional arrangement, mainstreaming of planning and budgeting activities, and data consolidation and reporting.

(ii) DENR endorsed, through a NSWMC resolution, a list of 4 NEAPP to be prohibited or phased out and listed 35 additional items for further study. (iii) DTI-BPS issued national standards to adopt international plastic product identification and established options for the recovery of plastic waste for recycling.

(i) DENR updated its Unified Fees and Charges through a DAO to include EPR-related services and activities to be collected by EMB. (ii) DENR issued interim guidelines on compliance reporting and audit for EPR with standards for accountable plastic footprint, accounted plastic waste diverted, and plastic waste diversion accomplishment.
Action 3: To harmonize and strengthen the role of LGUs across the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act, EPR, and NPOA-ML:
(i) The NSWMC of the DENR issued a resolution requiring LGUs to include in their forthcoming 10-year SWM plans: programs on marine litter prevention and management, existing partnerships with Obliged Enterprises, and plans and programs to support IWS. (ii) DILG issued a memorandum to facilitate the formalization and integration of the IWS into the solid waste management plans of the LGUs and formal solid waste sector in general.

(i) Guide its regional offices in the implementation of the NDC Gender Action Plan Policies and Measures based on the results of the gender assessment on waste sector and ensure alignment with national and international gender equality commitments. (ii) Require the EMB offices to implement the Policies and Measures in coordination with LGUs and communities, government agencies and private sector, which shall be funded by EMB's Gender and Development budget.

Action 1: To provide a system for the collection, compilation, and development of physical and natural capital accounts, the government enacted Republic Act No. 11995 or the PENCAS Act, and PSA issued the PENCAS IRR.
Action 2: To operationalize the key implementation mechanisms for PENCAS:
(i) PSA commenced generation of natural capital accounts and statistics under its Philippine Economic - Environmental and Natural Resources Accounts project. (ii) DENR issued a DAO that established the institutional mechanism for undertaking NCA in the DENR that provides for the development of DENR NCA Implementation Plan, the data management system for NCA ecosystems accounts, and the organizational setup of DENR for PENCAS implementation.
Action 3: To scale up implementation of blue carbon investments, DENR:
(i) Established the NBCAP with governance structure, allocated activities and proposed deliverables and timelines. (ii) Completed and launched a map of mangrove resources as part of its Geospatial National Database to support the identification, conservation, and ensuing investment in blue carbon resources.
Action 1: To implement key elements of the PENCAS Act and IRR:
(i) DENR will establish the NCA Information System for collection, management and compilation of environmental and economic data from various data producers for NCA and provide budget allocation for operation of the system. (ii) PSA will establish the ENREAS to be responsible for the development, enhancement, and implementation of natural capital and ecosystems accounts and progressively contribute to develop and generate natural capital-adjusted macro-economic indicators. (iii) DOF will establish NCA considerations for fiscal policies and regulations and develop incentive mechanisms that will drive natural capital investments. (iv) DEPDev will facilitate the inclusion of NCA in national and regional policy analysis, development planning, and investment programming.
Action 2: DEPDev will implement IMF C-PIMA recommendations for climate-responsive public investment in blue economy sectors. This may include:
(i) Providing guidance for developing and costing climate-resilient blue investment projects in the planning process informed by NCA tools. (ii) Incorporating climate-related mitigation and adaptation indicators for blue investments in the project appraisal process.
Action 3: DENR will approve a National Blue Carbon Roadmap and commence implementation, including:
(i) Mapping other blue carbon ecosystems and resources such as seagrass. (ii) Institutionalizing a carbon market policy framework in line with Article 6 of the Paris Agreement that includes encouraging protection, restoration, and management of blue carbon ecosystems and mitigating climate change. (iii) Adopting at least one bilateral government-to-government agreement in line with the framework incorporating blue carbon investment.

Policy 1: Integrated and inclusive management of coastal and marine ecosystems enabled Outcome 3: AUU fishponds identified for turnover or reversion to mangroves enhance natural protection buffer against climate-related risks
Action 2: To commence implementation of a national framework for blue economy development that adopts the ICM principles:
(i) DENR circulated a draft resolution and draft Joint Memorandum Circular to DILG, DA-BFAR, DOST and DHSUD which shall coordinate and clarify roles and commitments of agencies in blue economy development and ICM. (ii) DILG issued national guidelines for LGUs on the establishment, management, and protection of coastal greenbelts aligned with ICM principles. Base year: 2024 Base value: N Target date: 2025-09-30 Target value: Y
Action 3: To align national coastal and marine and biodiversity plans and targets with the Philippines' associated global commitments, DENR updated the abridged PBSAP in outlining specific key targets and indicators in line with the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework 2030. Base year: 2024 Base value: N Target date: 2025-09-30 Target value: Y
Action 4: To commence implementation of coastal resilience in line with the joint ICM and Blue Economy objectives through the protection and rehabilitation of mangroves in coastal areas:
(i) DENR and DA-BFAR signed an MOA to adopt an interdepartmental methodology for the assessment of public AUU Fishponds for prospective administrative reversion into mangrove areas. (ii) Department of Agriculture issued a regulation governing the lease of public lands for new fishponds to require mangrove-friendly aquaculture. (iii) DENR issued guidelines on the enrichment planting of mangroves and related activities for biodiversity conservation and coastal resiliency. Base year: 2024 Base value: N Target date: 2025-09-30 Target value: Y
Action 5: To enable productive and balanced management of fisheries resources and infrastructure:
(i) The Department of Agriculture, through BFAR, issued instructions for the implementation of Domestic Port Measures Enforcement integrating food safety, stock assessment data collection, and boat licensing and permitting. (ii) PFDA submitted to the Department of Agriculture a draft charter amendment to be considered for inclusion in the legislative agenda to extend PFDA's responsibilities to additional fisheries and agro-industrial commodities. Base year: 2024 Base value: N Target date: 2025-09-30 Target value: Y
Action 1: To formalize and embed the institutional framework for blue economy development, DENR will:
(i) Endorse the Blue Economy Bill for approval by Congress to establish a legal framework for national blue economy management. (ii) Adopt the National Ocean Environment Policy. (iii) Commence preparation of national and local marine spatial plans for blue economy development. Base year: 2024 Base value: N Target date: 2027-09-30 Target value: Y
